topic: Medium-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency Hypoketotic Hypoglycemia
stem: A 14-month-old girl is brought to the pediatric emergency department in a comatose state. Her parents report that she developed a mild viral gastroenteritis with vomiting 24 hours ago, during which she refused all oral intake and fluids. Physical examination reveals an unresponsive, hypotonic toddler with shallow respirations and mild hepatomegaly palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin. Bedside capillary glucose is 18 mg/dL. Immediate intravenous dextrose resuscitation restores consciousness over the next 30 minutes. Laboratory evaluation reveals: arterial pH 7.34, serum bicarbonate 18 mEq/L, serum ammonia 92 micromol/L (normal: 15–45 micromol/L), and serum AST 142 U/L and ALT 168 U/L. Urinalysis demonstrates 4+ glucose (post-resuscitation) and a complete absence of ketones (negative for acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate). Plasma acylcarnitine profile reveals markedly elevated octanoylcarnitine (C8) and hexanoylcarnitine (C6). Urine organic acid analysis reveals prominent dicarboxylic aciduria (adipic, suberic, and sebacic acids). The enzyme deficient in this patient catalyzes the initial reaction of which of the following metabolic pathways?

options.text: Peroxisomal very long-chain fatty acid oxidation coupled to molecular oxygen reduction to hydrogen peroxide
options.explanation: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation handles very long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs, >= C22) via acyl-CoA oxidase generating H2O2; defects cause X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ABCD1 mutation), not MCAD deficiency.

options.text: Hepatic mitochondrial ketogenesis converting acetoacetyl-CoA into 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA
options.explanation: HMG-CoA synthase catalyzes the condensation of acetoacetyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA in ketogenesis; while MCAD deficiency causes hypoketonemia, the enzymatic defect is in fatty acid beta-oxidation, starving ketogenesis of its substrate (acetyl-CoA).

options.text: Cytosolic carnitine biosynthesis from protein-bound lysine and methionine precursors
options.explanation: Primary carnitine deficiency (OCTN2 organic cation transporter mutation) impairs cellular carnitine uptake, presenting with low serum free carnitine, whereas MCAD deficiency features elevated acylcarnitines (especially C8).

options.text: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of fatty acids utilizing flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) as an electron acceptor
options.explanation: The child has Medium-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase (MCAD) deficiency, the most common inherited defect of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (autosomal recessive, frequently due to a c.985A>G mutation in the ACADM gene). In mitochondrial beta-oxidation, acyl-CoA dehydrogenases (VLCAD, LCAD, MCAD, SCAD) catalyze the initial dehydrogenation step, introducing a trans-double bond between C2 and C3 of fatty acyl-CoA, transferring electrons to FAD (producing FADH2, which transfers electrons to ubiquinone via electron-transferring flavoprotein). When hepatic glycogen is exhausted after a 12–18 hour fast, the liver relies on beta-oxidation of fatty acids to generate acetyl-CoA (which drives ketogenesis and allosterically activates pyruvate carboxylase for gluconeogenesis). In MCAD deficiency, medium-chain fatty acids (C6–C12) cannot be oxidized. The liver cannot synthesize ketones or maintain gluconeogenesis, producing catastrophic hypoketotic hypoglycemia, hyperammonemia, and hepatic steatosis. Excess medium-chain fatty acids undergo microsomal omega-oxidation, yielding C6–C10 dicarboxylic acids in urine.

options.text: Hepatic gluconeogenesis converting pyruvate into oxaloacetate via biotin carboxylation
options.explanation: Pyruvate carboxylase is a biotin-dependent gluconeogenic enzyme; in MCAD deficiency, pyruvate carboxylase is structurally normal but fails to be allosterically activated by acetyl-CoA.

topic: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia Kartagener Syndrome Dynein Arm Defect
stem: A 24-year-old man presents to the pulmonary clinic for evaluation of chronic productive cough with copious foul-smelling purulent sputum, recurrent sinusitis, and chronic nasal congestion. Since early childhood, he has experienced numerous episodes of pneumonia and otitis media. He also notes that he and his wife have been unable to conceive a child after 2 years of unprotected intercourse; semen analysis demonstrates normal sperm count but 0% sperm motility. Physical examination reveals bilateral inspiratory crackles over both lung bases, digital clubbing of both hands, and a cardiac apical impulse palpated in the right fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line (dextrocardia). Chest radiography confirms dextrocardia with the cardiac apex pointing to the right, along with gastric air bubble on the right side and liver shadow on the left (situs inversus totalis). High-resolution chest CT demonstrates bilateral saccular and cylindrical bronchiectasis in the middle and lower lung lobes. Nasal nitric oxide measurement is markedly reduced. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of a bronchial mucosal brush biopsy is most expected to demonstrate which of the following ultrastructural abnormalities in the respiratory ciliary axonemes?

options.text: Complete loss of the central pair of singlet microtubules with intact peripheral dynein arms
options.explanation: Central pair defects (such as transposition or absent central pair) account for <10% of PCD cases and do not typically exhibit situs inversus because embryonic nodal cilia normally have a "9 + 0" structure lacking the central pair.

options.text: Disruption of the apical zonula occludens tight junctions between respiratory epithelial cells
options.explanation: Zonula occludens (claudin/occludin) forms paracellular tight junctions; disruption alters barrier permeability but does not affect ciliary motility or sperm flagella.

options.text: Defective polymerization of desmin intermediate filaments anchoring basal bodies to the cytoskeleton
options.explanation: Desmin is a muscle-specific intermediate filament; ciliary basal bodies are anchored by tubulin and basal foot structures, not desmin.

options.text: Congenital absence of the CFTR chloride channel along the apical epithelial brush border
options.explanation: CFTR mutations cause cystic fibrosis, which presents with bronchiectasis and sinusitis, but CFTR is an apical chloride channel, not an axonemal motor protein, and does not cause situs inversus or absent dynein arms.

options.text: Absence of outer and inner dynein arms bridging adjacent peripheral microtubule doublets
options.explanation: The patient has Kartagener syndrome, a subset of primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) characterized by the clinical triad of: (1) situs inversus totalis; (2) chronic sinusitis; and (3) bronchiectasis, along with male infertility. Cilia and flagella share an identical ultrastructural core called the axoneme, composed of 9 peripheral microtubule doublets surrounding a central pair of single microtubules (the classic "9 + 2" arrangement). The outer and inner dynein arms contain dynein ATPase motor proteins that project from the A-tubule of each doublet toward the B-tubule of the adjacent doublet. ATP hydrolysis produces conformational sliding of adjacent doublets, translated into coordinated ciliary wave bending. In ~70% to 80% of PCD cases, mutations in dynein genes (e.g., DNAH5, DNAI1) result in complete absence or truncation of the dynein arms. Immotile cilia paralyze the mucociliary escalator (causing bronchiectasis and sinusitis). Defective nodal cilia in the embryonic primitive node disrupt leftward fluid flow during gastrulation, causing random 50/50 lateralization of visceral organs (situs inversus).

Confirmatory: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showing absent outer/inner dynein arms.
